study.title: Radial Wall Strain Assessment From AI-Assisted Angiography: Feasibility and Agreement With OCT as Reference Standard
study.venue: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

imaging.modality_detail: Dynamic coronary angiography (single angiographic projection) with coregistered OCT as reference
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries (LAD, diagonal, obtuse marginal, RCA); de novo lesions with 40-90% DS

public_dataset_used.detail: Lesions from a previous OCT FEA study

annotation.inter_rater_value: Interobserver ICC 0.88 (95% CI 0.81-0.92); intraobserver ICC 0.92 (95% CI 0.87-0.95) for repeated RWSAngio analysis

task.other_label: angiography-derived radial wall strain (biomechanical lumen deformation quantification)
task.task_description: Validation of AI-assisted angiography-derived radial wall strain (RWSAngio, from cyclic lumen diameter change over the cardiac cycle) against OCT-based finite element analysis RWS (RWSOCT); also identification of high-strain lesions.
task.clinical_application: Biomechanical assessment of coronary plaque vulnerability in the catheterization laboratory

temporal_evidence.quote: The lumen diameter change (LDC) at every longitudinal position along the interrogated lesion was then computed as the maximal diameter over the cardiac cycle minus the minimal diameter over the cardiac cycle.

metrics.metric: Lin concordance coefficient RWSAngio vs RWSOCT
Lin concordance coefficient LDCAngio vs LDCOCT
Exact match of maximal RWS location
Maximal RWS locations within half lesion length
Mean RWSAngio analysis time per lesion

code_available.detail: Commercially available software (AngioPlus Core, Pulse Medical)

G3.quote: compute the dynamic changes of luminal deformation over the cardiac cycle

G4.quote: the projection-dependent calculation of RWSAngio especially for asymmetric lesions

other_limitations: Proportional and constant bias of RWSAngio versus RWSOCT
Systematic differences between OCT and angiography in lumen diameter quantification
Cardiac motion artefacts included in RWSAngio but excluded from OCT FEA
future_work: Prospective studies with angiograms systematically acquired at optimal projections
Projection optimization using coronary CT or angiography-based viewing angle optimization
Combining RWSAngio with angiography-based physiological assessment for risk stratification
Investigating safety of deferring stenting in non-flow-limiting stenoses with low RWSAngio
Targeted intracoronary imaging for stenoses with high RWSAngio
